description: We are students at Tecnológico de Monterrey, San Luis Potosí campus, and members of the GameTechMX student group. Our project, FRONTIER: Mission Control Academy, aims to teach NASA science through collaborative gameplay. Our participation is part of a student initiative exploring the feasibility of introducing Amazon Future Engineer in Mexico and expanding access to technology education.
summary:
FRONTIER: Mission Architect is a functional educational space exploration game developed in Java by GameTech Frontier MX for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.

Players become mission architects, designing spacecraft with a low-poly construction system before launching from Earth toward three destinations: Mars, Jupiter, and Miller, a fictional world inspired by science fiction. Each destination offers a different playable scientific mission. On Mars, players operate a rover to collect geological samples and recover them using a remotely controlled spacecraft. At Jupiter, players investigate atmospheric conditions and map the planet from orbit. On Miller, players explore a hypothetical environment in search of biological evidence.

Through spacecraft construction, exploration, and mission objectives, FRONTIER introduces young people to the challenges of planning space missions and balancing scientific goals with engineering decisions. Our goal is to transform complex space science concepts into an accessible, interactive STEM learning experience that inspires the next generation of explorers.
details:
FRONTIER: Mission Architect

The Problem

Space mission design involves complex decisions related to spacecraft construction, scientific instruments, energy, mass, communication systems, and limited resources. For many young students, these concepts can be difficult to understand through traditional learning methods.

Our Solution

FRONTIER: Mission Architect is an educational video game designed to introduce students to space mission engineering through interactive exploration and decision-making. Instead of only observing a spacecraft, players take the role of mission architects who must plan their exploration strategy, configure their vehicles, and complete scientific objectives.

Gameplay Concept

The game begins on Earth, where players select their destination and design a spacecraft using a simplified low-poly construction system.

The project includes three mission scenarios:

Mission 1 — Mars: Players explore the Martian environment using a rover, collect a geological sample, and operate a remote spacecraft to recover the scientific material while avoiding obstacles.

Mission 2 — Jupiter: Players investigate Jupiter's atmosphere, collect scientific measurements, and generate an atmospheric map from orbit. They must plan how to retrieve or transmit their scientific results.

Mission 3 — Miller: Players explore a fictional ocean world inspired by science fiction. This mission introduces hypothetical astrobiology research and environmental challenges while distinguishing fictional elements from established NASA science.

Educational Approach

The project is designed around the relationship between engineering decisions and mission performance. Students are encouraged to consider spacecraft mass, available energy, scientific instruments, mission objectives, and operational limitations. The intended learning experience demonstrates that a successful space mission requires balancing scientific ambition with engineering feasibility.

Technology

The game is being developed using Java and a low-poly visual style, with an emphasis on accessible gameplay and interactive spacecraft construction.

Innovation and Impact

FRONTIER: Mission Architect combines game-based learning, spacecraft design, and scientific exploration in an experience intended for young students. Our objective is to encourage interest in STEM education by transforming abstract engineering concepts into interactive challenges. The project aims to inspire future scientists, programmers, and engineers while introducing them to the principles behind real space missions.
